picked.t: [베트남 주간 이슈] 12년 걸린 고속도로 개통에 증시 대통합까지…베트남에 '판'이 깔린다
picked.body: 호치민시의 3분기 경제성장률(GRDP)이 10년 만에 최고치인 10%에 육박하고, 착공 12년 만에 남부 물류의 핵심인 고속도로 전 구간이 뚫렸다. 베트남 시장의 판도가 근본적으로 바뀌고 있다. 단순히 저임금 노동력을 노리던 시대는 끝났다. 삼성전기는 AI 기판, LS에코에너지는 방산용 희토류, 두산에너빌리티는 대형 에너지 인프라를 쓸어 담으며 베트남을 첨단 기술의 핵심 거점으로 탈바꿈시키고 있다.  여기에 299개 종목의 증시 일괄 이전과 엄격해진 규제 환경까지 맞물리며 '진짜 실력'을 겨루는 판이 깔렸다.  베트남 주간 경제·산업 동향 포인트 3가지 1. 대규모 인프라 및 친환경 에너지벨트 구축 가속화 롱탄신공항 개항 준비와 벤륵-롱탄 고속도로 전 구간 개통 등 대형 교통망 확충이 본궤도에 올랐다. 또한 2029년부터 전기차 배터리 재활용 의무화가 추진되는 등 친환경 기준이 엄격해진다. 2. 한국 대기업들의 첨단·에너지·소재 분야 대규모 투자 러시 삼성전기의 AI 기판 증설, LS에코에너지의 희토류 생산거점 구축, 두산에너빌리티의 화력발전 및 가스복합 수주 등 전통 제조업을 넘어선 첨단 기술과 에너지 협력이 두드러진다.  3. 디지털 경제·이커머스 중심의 내수 시장 고도화 이커머스와 SNS 쇼핑이 명절 성수기 매출을 견인하고 생성형 AI 사용률이 급증하는 등 베트남 소비 시장의 디지털 전환이 빠르게 진행되고 있다. ■ 행정부·정치·정책 '규제 고도화와 친환경 기준 강화' 베트남과 캐나다가 양국 관계를 ‘전략적 동반자 관계’로 격상하며 경제 및 외교적 협력 범위를 대폭 확대했다. 외국인 및 기관이 현지 근로자 구인 시 ‘국가고용플랫폼’에 채용공고를 게시하는 것이 의무화되어 고용 투명성이 높아진다. 2029년부터 판매량 기준 최소 8% 이상의 전기차 배터리 재활용이 의무화되며 친환경 규제가 구체화되고 있다. ■ 매크로·산업·경제 '수출 회복세와 디지털 소비 확산' 9월 제조업 PMI는 51.9로 전월 대비 1.4포인트 하락하며 경기 회복세가 다소 주춤한 모습을 보였다. 새우 수출이 8월 기준 33억 달러로 전년 동기 대비 12% 증가하는 등 농수산물 수출이 호조를 기록했다. 이커머스 쇼피와 틱톡숍의 월병 합산 매출이 1,600억 동에 육박하며 온라인 유통의 영향력이 급증했다. ■ 기업·금융·부동산 '전통 대기업의 신사업 진출과 증시 통합' 빈그룹이 1조 동 규모의 석유·가스 법인을 신설하며 신사업 진출에 박차를 가하고 있다. 하노이증권거래소의 모든 종목이 12월 말 호치민증권거래소로 이전 상장되며 자본시장 효율성이 강화된다. 미래에셋파이낸스 베트남이 중앙은행으로부터 예금 및 결제계좌 신규 사업 승인을 받아 핀테크 영토를 확장했다. ■ 인프라·하노이·호치민시 '교통망 완공과 메가시티 성장' 착공 12년 만에 ‘벤륵-롱탄 고속도로’ 전 구간이 개통되며 남부 경제권의 물류 효율성이 대폭 향상됐다. 호치민시의 3분기 GRDP 성장률이 10%에 육박하며 10년 만에 최고치를 기록했다. 하노이와 호치민시가 ‘디지털노마드’를 위한 세계 최고의 도시 상위 10위권에 진입했다. ■ 사회·한-베 이슈 '첨단 협력 확대와 다각적 진출' LS에코에너지가 베트남에 '방산용 희토류' 생산거점을 구축하며 핵심 광물 공급망 협력을 강화한다. HS효성이 다낭에 1억 달러 규모의 BCF 원사·카펫 생산공장을 착공하며 베트남 투자를 지속하고 있다. 두산에너빌리티가 8,380억 원 규모의 화력발전소 EPC 계약을 체결하는 등 에너지 인프라 수주를 이어갔다.

picked.t: Dollar up against dong on black market
picked.body: The greenback gained 0.27% to around VND26,030 at unofficial exchange points. The currency was firm at VND26,170 at lender Vietcombank. The State Bank of Vietnam increased its reference rate by 0.02% to VND25,643. Globally, the euro weakened sharply on Monday to a 17-month low as fiscal worries in France amid a steep bond market rout stoked fears of contagion risks in the region, helping the dollar shrug off soft US jobs ‌data that dented near-term rate hike expectations, Reuters reported. The euro slid to as low as $1.1161, its weakest level since May 2025 in Asian hours after clocking four straight weekly declines. Sterling slipped 0.24% to $1.32064, while the Japanese yen changed hands at 157.92 per dollar. That left the dollar index, which measures the US currency against six major units, up 0.47% at 102.37. "The dollar is the main winner in the current environment as not only is the rise in Treasury yields boosting the appeal of US ‌assets, but ⁠the broad selloff in debt globally is fuelling safe-haven flows into the greenback," said Matthew Ryan, head of market strategy at Ebury.

picked.t: Dulux paintmaker to sell Southeast Asia paints business to Nippon Paint for $1.35B
picked.body: The sale covers decorative paints operations in Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand, Singapore, Papua New Guinea and Australia, the Dutch paints maker said, adding that it expects net cash proceeds of about $1 billion after tax and payments to minority partners. The Dulux paintmaker earlier divested its decorative paints operations in India and Pakistan for $1.6 billion and 50 million euros, respectively. "The successful completion of our Asia portfolio review is part of an ongoing strategy to focus our portfolio on areas where we can achieve differentiating scale and strengthen our position," AkzoNobel Chief Executive Greg Poux-Guillaume said in a statement. The Indonesia deal is expected to close separately in late 2026, while the remaining transactions are expected to close around mid-2027. AkzoNobel said it will now focus on the successful closing of its merger with U.S. coatings maker Axalta, which was announced in November last year. Nippon Paint submitted multiple proposals to acquire AkzoNobel's decorative paints business, the Dutch company said in July, valuing it at about EUR7.5 billion ($8.44 billion). That approach followed the withdrawal of a EUR12.5 billion bid for the entire company that Nippon Paint had pursued jointly with U.S.-based paintmaker Sherwin-Williams in June. The Financial Times , which earlier reported the Southeast Asia deal, said Nippon remains interested in a larger deal for the decorative paint business, but that integration of the Southeast Asia business could occupy the company for some time and AkzoNobel does not have plans to sell further assets from the business.

picked.t: Starting over at 50: Why more middle-aged Vietnamese are embracing second careers
picked.body: In Dong Nai Province, Nguyen Anh Van once served as an army lieutenant colonel. To outsiders, he enjoyed enviable career stability and merely had to run out the clock until retirement. But beneath that security lay a persistent unease, a gnawing conviction that he had chosen the wrong path. His outlook shifted in 2006 when an assignment as a military lay assessor on a court-martial bench ignited a deep interest in the law. Shortly after, he began balancing his military duties with coursework, eventually earning a bachelor of laws degree in 2014. In 2021, after completing 28 years in uniform, Van applied for early retirement under his unit's downsizing initiative. "I hesitated at the time because walking away from a secure job was daunting, and with no civilian work experience, I had no clue how I would make ends meet out in the world," he recalls. After waiting 14 months for the official paperwork approving his retirement at age 47, he set a strict personal rule never to touch his pension, saving the entire amount for his two children. In early 2022, as the Covid-19 pandemic receded, he enrolled in a 12-month professional legal training program at the Judicial Academy before serving a mandatory one-year apprenticeship. To cover tuition and living costs, the former officer drove motorbike taxis, delivered packages, took on freelance typing gigs, and never gave up his ritual of reading late into the night. Stepping back into a campus at nearly 50 proved no obstacle for a veteran conditioned by military discipline. At 4:30 a.m. each day, he dedicated 90 minutes to exercise, using his morning workouts and coffee breaks to pore over case files and statutory codes. By channeling decades of practical life experience into legal problem-solving, he cleared the rigorous bar apprenticeship exam, a hurdle that trips up 60 to 70 percent of test-takers. In late 2025, upon being admitted to the bar, he joined a law firm in Bien Hoa Ward located in the southern province of Dong Nai. He opted for a per-case compensation model across civil, commercial, criminal, and family law disputes, while routinely providing pro bono defense for disadvantaged clients. In a recent criminal case, his close examination of the filings revealed procedural missteps and unconvincing evidence gathered by investigators. The court upheld his argument, remanding the case back to authorities for further investigation. Outside the courtroom, his emotional maturity has helped mediate settlements for several couples considering divorce. "Seeing the smiles and grateful embraces from a client's family reassures me that I chose the right path," the 51-year-old says. "A day has 24 hours; as long as you live in good health and create value, that is more than enough." Phuong Mai, a 50-year-old banking professional in Hanoi, recently graduated with a practitioner degree in traditional medicine and an associate degree in pharmacology after six years of balancing a full-time job with evening classes. To free up time for mandatory hospital clinical work, she arranged an alternate work schedule at her bank. On many days, she would rush straight from office to the lecture hall, and from class directly to hospital wards, trimming lunch down to 15 minutes to preserve an hour for working out. Mai's drive took root over a decade ago following a family crisis, when her mother fell seriously ill right after retiring, a collapse compounded by years of caring for a relative who had been bedridden for 11 years following a stroke. Pursuing medical studies also allowed her to revive a four-generation family healing tradition that was at risk of dying out. "Growing up with my maternal grandfather, I absorbed the principle that food is medicine and that prevention always trumps cure," she says. "I wanted to build this foundation for a second career so I could care for my own health and support others." Van and Mai's trajectories epitomize the emerging "encore career" trend, a term coined by American scholar Marc Freedman to describe purposeful work pursued during the second half of life. Unlike casual post-retirement odd jobs aimed solely at covering daily living expenses or as a brief hiatus before fully stepping away, an encore career typically spans 10 to 20 years, bringing together one or more of dependable income, personal fulfillment, and an enduring desire to serve society. Tran Bang Viet, CEO of business consulting and management training firm Dong A Solutions, says this movement reflects more than just the personal desires of older workers but meets the corporate need for deep domain expertise. In an era shaped by artificial intelligence, where general knowledge is readily accessible, the unique edge of veteran professionals lies in tacit knowledge forged through decades of hands-on experience, he says.
